subject: Business Models
title: Quibi: The $1.75 Billion Flop
description: A 60-second lesson on Quibi: The $1.75 Billion Flop.

hook.text: Quibi raised $1.75 billion for 10-minute premium video episodes. It shut down after 6 months.

buildup.text: Jeffrey Katzenberg bet that people wanted Hollywood-quality short videos on their phones. TikTok was already free.

discovery.text: Quibi launched during COVID when people were at home watching full-length content, not quick mobile bites.

twist.text: Quibi couldn't be screenshot or shared. It blocked the virality that TikTok and YouTube thrived on.

climax.text: Quibi proved that high budgets can't beat free user-generated content. Hollywood polish lost to TikTok authenticity.

punchline.text: $1.75 billion, 6 months, zero cultural impact. Expensive content lost to free.

quiz.question: Why did Quibi fail despite massive funding?
options: It competed with free, shareable content and launched during COVID lockdowns

details.summary: Quibi raised 1.75 billion dollars to create premium short-form video content for mobile viewing, launching in April 2020. Despite Hollywood talent and massive funding, it attracted fewer than 500,000 paying subscribers and shut down after just six months.
details.whyItMatters: Quibi proved that capital and celebrity content cannot guarantee product-market fit. Free platforms like TikTok and YouTube already dominated short-form mobile video, making a premium paid service unnecessary regardless of production quality.
takeaways: 1.75 billion dollars in funding could not overcome lack of product-market fit
Free short-form video on TikTok and YouTube made paid content unnecessary
Quibi shut down just six months after launch with fewer than 500K subscribers

faq.question: Why did Quibi fail despite raising 1.75 billion dollars?
faq.answer: No product-market fit. People already watched short videos free on TikTok and YouTube. Quibi's mobile-only approach prevented sharing content socially. Launching during COVID lockdowns when people preferred big-screen viewing at home made the mobile-first format even less appealing.

faq.question: What lessons does Quibi's failure teach about content businesses?
faq.answer: Distribution matters more than content quality. Social sharing is essential for discovery. Free alternatives cap willingness to pay. Customer behavior validation should precede massive investment. Even Hollywood talent cannot create demand that consumer habits do not support.
